    Chains, Harada–Sai, and an Auslander-type theorem #

    Chain P n c: c is a composite of n non-bijective maps between objects satisfying P. If P-objects are indecomposable of dimension ≤ b, a chain of length 2ᵇ − 1 is zero (Chain.eq_zero).

    RASFam P X: a right almost split family into X with sources in P.

    auslander: if every P-object has such a family and every nonzero module maps nonzero into some P-object, then every indecomposable module is isomorphic to a P-object.

        ∃ (X : FDMod k A), P X ∧ ∃ (f : N ⟶ X), Function.Bijective ⇑(FDMod.lin f)

        An Auslander-type theorem. If the indecomposable objects P of bounded dimension have right almost split families inside P, and every nonzero module maps nonzero into some P-object, then every indecomposable module is isomorphic to a P-object.
